newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda says will offer new suspension.
newsitem.headline: Honda says will offer new suspension.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd announced on Wednesday that it will offer a new suspension, a fuel-saving power-assisted steering system and an improved wheel-control system on some of its new models to be launched in Japan in the autumn.
It did not say what models, but industry sources said they were likely to include the Accord, Honda's mainstay.
Honda said its new double wishbone rear suspension increases driving stability and comfort while allowing more passenger and trunk space.
Also offered will be an electric power-assisted steering system, which Honda said will cut fuel consumption by three percent to five percent over mechanically power-assisted steering systems.
Conventional mechanically power-assisted steering constantly draw power from the engine, even when steering wheel is not being turned.
Honda expects the news steering system to replace power-assisted steering systems in the next five to 10 years, the Honda official said.
Honda also said it would be offering a better anti-lock brake system which cuts down on skids in rainy or snowy conditions.
